sections.heading: Content Modes
sections.body: Use the three modes to match content surface and length for Sky, Horoscope, and feed contexts.

items.label: Feed Mode
items.body: 1 to 2 short paragraphs. Prioritize current lived effect, specific timing, and one practical move. Use this for daily transits and brief check-in summaries.

items.label: In-Depth Mode
items.body: 3 to 5 paragraphs. Explain mechanism, observable behavior, practical implications by life area, and the integration path. Use for major placements, transits, and relationship pattern entries.

items.label: Article Mode
items.body: Long-form essay style with clear sections, collective context, and reflective close. Use for eclipses, New Moons, Full Moons, and seasonal cycles with household and ritual framing.

sections.heading: Sky Card Structure
sections.body: Write each Sky output with this order: headline, what this feels like, why this is happening, what to do, and timing. Keep the headline factual and astronomy-linked.

sections.heading: Lunar Event Templates
sections.body: Match structure to event type and phase intensity. For brief entries, keep only the strongest two lines for each section.

items.label: New Moon
items.body: Open with phase and sign. Include six-month arc, two-week arc, intention framing, and the exact release condition when the arc matures.

items.label: Full Moon
items.body: Open with culmination and release frame. Show what has become visible since the corresponding New Moon and what can be released with integrity.

items.label: Eclipse
items.body: Use witness-first language. Avoid prediction language. Name the turning point and where identity, relationship, or direction is being redefined.

sections.heading: Planetary Layering
sections.body: Report event facts and the strongest active transit overlays only. If multiple transits compete, include a second overlay only when it materially changes tone or action.

sections.heading: Sign and House Linking
sections.body: If a phase has a natal-house link, include house themes in plain language only when the link is materially clear in the timing window.

sections.heading: Tone Guide
sections.body: No em dashes. No prediction certainty. Use soft modality. Start from observed experience, then explanation, then action. Close with what becomes possible.
